question: Does this change earn a CHANGELOG bullet? Answer user-visible when someone using the published version of the extension would notice it (new or changed behavior, a fixed defect they could hit, a moved shortcut or action). Answer internal when nothing a user sees changes (refactors, tests, comments, tooling, build configuration). Answer branch-only-bug when it fixes or reverts something that existed only on this unpublished branch, so the published version never had the defect.

change.description: the change, in one or two sentences

context.description: what is known about whether the published version had the behavior

inputs.change: Fix three quadratic paths in wrap and unwrap: an 833 KB single paragraph took 18,031 ms and 1 MB of prose took 32,056 ms; after the fix they take 22 ms and 39 ms.
inputs.context: Three of the four slow paths shipped to the Store in the initial submission and stayed live across two releases. Nobody filed an issue, because a 32-second freeze reads to a user as Raycast hanging.

inputs.change: Pinning a migrated zero-turn conversation no longer deletes it: persistFilter now gates only rows that were absent from storage before the write.
inputs.context: The defect came from the shared collection store and the legacy-data migration, both introduced by a 39-commit storage refactor on a branch that was never merged.

inputs.change: Restore Sort by Popularity to Shift-Command-P after an earlier release moved it to Shift-Command-S.
inputs.context: Shift-Command-P is a long-standing user shortcut. The move to Shift-Command-S answered a reviewer's collision finding that turned out to be false, and it shipped; this change moves the shortcut back.

inputs.change: Bound the block-safety probe in wrap to the tokens that can land on the candidate line, instead of joining every remaining token per rejected break.
inputs.context: The unbounded version was the first cut of a review-round-7 correctness fix; on 1 MB of prose it took 32,056 ms. That code never reached a commit, so no published version had it.

inputs.change: Replace the ad hoc per-hook persistence rules with one shared collection store and an explicit migration path for legacy data.
inputs.context: A 39-commit storage refactor of the extension; the commit itself replaces how hooks persist, not what they show.

inputs.change: Add a performance guard test that fails when wrapping 1 MB of prose exceeds its time budget.
inputs.context: The guard caught a 32,056 ms regression in a first cut of a correctness fix before that code reached a commit; the guard itself is a test.
